title: Folded-cascode OTA
topology: A single-stage OTA that combines the output-impedance boost of cascoding with a wider input/output common-mode range than a stacked (telescopic) cascode by 'folding' the differential pair's signal current from one device type (e.g. NMOS input pair) into cascode transistors of the opposite type (PMOS), each folding node fed by its own DC current source rather than by a purely stacked device chain. The two folded branches' currents are combined at a cascoded current mirror to produce a single-ended, high-impedance output. DC gain is approximately gm_in times the parallel combination of the two folded branches' cascoded output resistances (each on the order of gm*ro^2), roughly two orders of magnitude higher than the bare five-transistor OTA's single gm*ro.
spec_class: moderate-to-high-gain, wide-common-mode-range single-stage OTA — the core gain stage in switched-capacitor circuits (SAR/pipeline ADC residue amplifiers, sample-and-hold buffers) and general feedback amplifiers where a two-stage op-amp's extra compensation complexity is undesirable

pdk_portability.notes: The folded topology and cascode-current-source biasing scheme are portable to any PDK with adequate supply headroom for the four-to-five stacked/folded device drops it requires; the specific cascode bias-voltage generation and the achievable output swing are sky130-specific, since they depend on sky130's threshold voltages and available supply rails (commonly 1.8V core), which bound how many devices can be stacked in the folding branches before headroom loss becomes the limiting factor on output swing.

sizing_approach: Size the input differential pair for the required input-referred noise and transconductance using a gm/ID design point; size the folding current sources so each folding branch's DC current stays comfortably above the maximum expected signal current from the input pair, so no cascode transistor is starved (cut off) under large differential input swings; size the cascode devices for adequate drain-source saturation-voltage headroom rather than for maximum intrinsic gain, since output swing is usually the binding constraint in a folded-cascode stage at low supply voltages; size the output cascode current mirror for a 1:1 ratio (or a modest step-up within compliance to trade area for gain); add wide-swing (low-voltage) cascode bias generation at reduced supply voltages to recover output swing that a simple high-swing cascode-bias scheme would otherwise sacrifice.
layout_idioms: input differential pair in common-centroid layout, matched to the same discipline as a five-transistor OTA input pair, plus matched and interdigitated cascode transistor pairs on each folding branch
folding-current-source transistors laid out as unit cells with dummy devices, matched to the differential-pair unit cells so the folding-branch current ratio holds across process gradients
cascode bias ladder placed adjacent to the amplifier core with short, symmetric bias routing to each cascode gate, avoiding systematic mismatch from IR drop or capacitive coupling into the bias nets
output cascode current mirror interdigitated and common-centroid-matched identically to a five-transistor OTA's mirror load for accurate current-ratio matching

source.citation: K. Bult and G. J. G. M. Geelen, "A fast-settling CMOS op amp for SC circuits with 90-dB DC gain," IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits, vol. 25, no. 6, pp. 1379-1384, Dec. 1990.
source.license_or_openness: Peer-reviewed IEEE journal paper cited here for its folded-cascode topology and settling/gain trade-off methodology only (no figures or text reproduced), per the KB's open-sources sourcing rule (case 2, peer-reviewed paywalled literature cited for restated methodology only, in kb/SOURCING.md). This is a widely-cited reference establishing the folded-cascode op amp as a high-DC-gain, fast-settling alternative to a two-stage design for switched-capacitor applications.

notes: Framed here as a general-purpose folded-cascode gain stage rather than the full 90 dB / gain-boosted amplifier the source paper builds; gain-boosting (auxiliary local feedback amplifiers around each cascode) is a common further extension when gm*ro^2-scale gain is insufficient, but adds its own stability considerations and is out of scope for this entry. Because it remains a single dominant-pole stage, a folded-cascode OTA is often easier to compensate in a feedback loop than a two-stage Miller design, at the cost of the extra folding-branch bias current the topology requires.
